name: Andersonville Prison
scope: Present physical reconstructions of Andersonville Prison: both short stockade sections (northgate with rectangular two-gate sallyport and northeast L-corner), their roofed sentry platforms, diagonal-board gate leaves/wicket and short low deadline rail. No invented standing 1864 whole enclosure, barracks or prisoner tents. Separate museum/cemetery/monuments/Providence Spring shelter/Star Fort and general park landscape are excluded.

originalReview.notes: StarFort earthen battery with two display cannons, mown grassy floor, low earthwork banks and wooded edge. Does not depict a surviving enclosed prison building or measured whole fort earthwork.
Northeast stockade: tall close-set rounded/hewn vertical timber wall, horizontal stiffening rail, roofed open sentry platform on two tall outer posts; gray weathered pine.
Inside sallyport: two tall timber sidewalls, closed diagonally boarded double gate with pedestrian wicket/iron straps, high log wall above lintel, two roofed open sentry platforms.
Exterior northgate: short stockade main wall with projecting rectangular two-gate sallyport, weathered vertical pine logs/uneven crowns, sloping site and roofed open sentry platform.
